## Summary

DMACON2, INTENA2 and INTREQ2 control DMA and interrupts of Arne audio channels 4–15 and of the Ethernet. Bit n is channel n + 4; bit 13 is Ethernet.

## Details

### Registers

| Address | Name | Access | Description (original) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$DFF202` | DMACON2 Read | R | – |
| `$DFF21C` | INTENA2 Read | R | – |
| `$DFF21E` | INTREQ2 Read | R | – |
| `$DFF296` | DMACON2 | W | DMACON2 |
| `$DFF29A` | INTENA2 | W | INTENA2 |
| `$DFF29C` | INTREQ2 | W | INTREQ2 |

- `$DFF21C`: corrected: upper case, as everywhere else.

### INTENA2 and INTREQ2

Both use the same bits. INTREQ2 needs a set and a clear write to load arbitrary data, as INTREQ (original).

| Bits | Function | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 15 |  | SET/CLR |
| 14 |  |  |
| 13 | ETH | Ethernet |
| 12 |  |  |
| 11 | AUD15 | Audio channel 15 block finished |
| 10 | AUD14 | Audio channel 14 block finished |
| 9 | AUD13 | Audio channel 13 block finished |
| 8 | AUD12 | Audio channel 12 block finished |
| 7 | AUD11 | Audio channel 11 block finished |
| 6 | AUD10 | Audio channel 10 block finished |
| 5 | AUD9 | Audio channel 9 block finished |
| 4 | AUD8 | Audio channel 8 block finished |
| 3 | AUD7 | Audio channel 7 block finished |
| 2 | AUD6 | Audio channel 6 block finished |
| 1 | AUD5 | Audio channel 5 block finished |
| 0 | AUD4 | Audio channel 4 block finished |

The original adds:

- "Ethernet will throw IRQ $48"
- "The new Audio channels will throw IRQ $50"

Whether `$48` and `$50` are vector offsets or vector numbers, and at which interrupt level they arrive, is an open question (see [index.md](index.md)).

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- Classic DMACON/INTENA/INTREQ cover audio channels 0–3 only. Channels 0–3 stay there on SAGA; the second set adds 4–15 and Ethernet.

## Do / Don't

- DO use bit 15 as SET/CLR, as in the classic registers.
- DO map channel n (4–15) to bit n − 4.
